positive: Second subword piece of rare multi-token proper names/Latin or Greek terms, especially 'psilon' in 'Upsilon Andromedae' (astronomy star names with Greek-letter prefixes) and mid-word pieces of species binomials (e.g. 'gam-mar-us'). Wikipedia science articles.
negative: Ordinary English function/content words in release/publication contexts: subword 'lease' in 're-release', space or 'with' after 'released in'/'Beginning', counts like '3 major'. Media/entertainment (games, films, albums) release-history prose.

positive: The day-of-month digit token in a date: the digit right before or as part of a day number followed by a month name ('on 1[1] November', 'on 1[2] September') or after a month name ('March [4] ,'), also 'night of [4] / 5'. Calendar dates in Wikipedia history prose.
negative: Leading digit '1' of quantities like 100, 120, 126 in non-date numeric contexts: percent denominators '/100', 'out of 100', '\times' results, tempos 'tempo of 126'. Especially math reasoning with percentages and money.

positive: ' City' completing 'New York City' (place-name completion after 'New York'); also single capital variable letters in math setup ('Let $S$').
negative: Markdown/formatting tokens in model reasoning: 'Response:**', indentation whitespace before bullets, sentence-ending periods in math reasoning; also subword continuations like 'ariat' in Secretariat, ' States' at line start.

positive: Preposition or modifier right after a noun/adjective in academic/scientific register, linking to research/science concepts: 'area[ of] academic research', 'undesirable[ from] an efficiency standpoint', 'addition[ to] the repertoire', 'a[ scientific] demonstration', 'Committee on[ Research]'. Chemistry/science-research prose.
negative: Mid-word subword pieces inside proper names, years and technical terms: digit inside a year ('1[9]97'), 'aut' in tautomerization, 'antasy' in Phantasy, 'ot' in bioterror, ' Planet' in Planetpol. Fragmentary tokens of named entities.

positive: Token right after a subject/clause transition in narrative review/biographical prose: verbs after plural/proper subject ('critics[ were]', 'but[ was]'), and first-name/initial pieces of personal or place names ('Paul[ A].', 'Hervey[ Ben]ham', 'at[ Men]in Road').
negative: Tokens in definitional/logical statements and math reasoning conclusions: 'is[ not] bound', 'the final[ answer]', 'the[ result] is an integer', 'a[ rigid] definition', closing parentheses after lists. Abstract/analytical predicate words.

positive: Capitalized first letter token beginning a personal or place name (especially non-English names split into initial-letter + rest: ' M'erv, ' N'iall, ' G'idō, ' N'ijō), often after a title/role word or in a list of names.
negative: Single capital letters that are model/product designators, musical keys, or letter-names rather than starts of names: 'Lola[ T]620', 'key of[ C] minor', 'The[ X] Factor', 'A[ T].G.I.', 'Soviet-made[ T]-54'. Letter + number/code.

positive: Weak: structural tokens in step-by-step lists - 'Step' headers in markdown reasoning, newline before bullets, list commas/'and' between names in prose lists.
negative: Separators ( ' +', ',') inside long repetitive math sequences/enumerations: '7 + 7 + 7 + 7[ +]', '\theta_3[,]', '14th[,] 15', 'a_4^2[ +] a_5'. Repeated arithmetic/indexed series in LaTeX or ordinal lists.

positive: Clothing/fashion and pageant/venue nouns, often subword pieces: 'page'ant, le'ot'ard, sleeveless[ white] blouse, Madison[ Square] Garden. Descriptions of outfits and performances (Madonna, Miss America).
negative: Product-line/collection nouns following a brand or category: cosmetics[ line], Colour[ Collection], Kids[ range], 3D Classics[ line], Art[ Direction]. Merchandise/product-range and credit-role terms.

positive: Second subword piece of fictional character/place names from anime/fantasy franchises, especially Naruto (Kon[oha], Kak[ashi], Sas[uke]) and Harry[ Potter]. Pop-culture fictional names.
negative: Weak: completion of real-world proper names (Eddie[ Murphy], Niall[ Stokes], Jamie[ Fo]xx, Man[as] Air Base) and product numbers (Windows [2]000).

positive:
Paragraph/line breaks ('

', '
') following a completed sentence or heading in model step-by-step math reasoning, right before a new bullet or numbered step; also sentence-final periods ending a reasoning sentence.
negative: Tokens opening inline math or markdown: ' **' bold heading start, ' $(' and ' $\' LaTeX openers, ' equals' after a LaTeX expression; also suffixes like 'ist' in Maoist.
